features.description: Grader interface — one typed contract returning a verdict, a reason, the artifact inspected, and which component the evidence came from
steps: Define a frozen result type carrying: verdict, a human-readable reason, the artifact path or identifier inspected, the grader id, and the component the evidence came from so a harness bug is distinguishable from a system finding
Define the grader call signature: it receives one trial record plus a handle to that trial's produced artifacts, and returns one or more results
Graders are pure with respect to the run — they read artifacts and never write, mutate, or re-invoke the supervisor
A grader that cannot evaluate returns an explicit not-applicable verdict rather than a pass, so absence never reads as success
Scope stops at the contract; concrete graders are F002 to F004
features.acceptance: (1) A grader that attempts to write to the artifacts it was given fails a purity test that monkeypatches the write paths. (2) A grader returning a result omitting a required field is rejected at construction. (3) A grader with no opinion returns not-applicable and the aggregate distinguishes that from a pass. (4) Every result names the component its evidence came from. (5) pytest tests/test_grader_interface.py covers all four and passes.

features.description: Artifact-conformance graders — schema validity of produced plan artifacts, and evidence discipline on any feature flipped to passing
steps: Schema grader runs the existing validator over every plan artifact a trial produced and reports the failing pointer rather than a bare boolean
Evidence grader requires a feature flipped to passing to carry the verifier, the timestamp, and at least one evidence reference the schema already demands
Both run offline with no model call
Neither grader writes to the artifacts it inspects
features.acceptance: (1) A trial producing an artifact missing a required frontmatter key is failed with that key named. (2) A trial flipping a feature to passing with an empty evidence list is failed. (3) A clean trial passes both. (4) pytest tests/test_conformance_graders.py covers all three and passes.

features.description: Consistency graders — gate state agreeing with the recorded event log, and no file written outside the repositories the plan declares
steps: Gate agreement grader requires every gate recorded cleared in gate state to have a matching event naming the same actor, and fails when either side carries a gate the other lacks
Target-boundary grader compares files written during a trial against the repositories the plan's Target section declares
Both run offline with no model call
The boundary grader reports the offending path rather than only a count
features.acceptance: (1) A trial whose gate state records a cleared gate absent from the event log is failed. (2) The reverse case, an event with no corresponding gate-state entry, is also failed. (3) A trial writing outside every declared repository is failed with the path named. (4) A clean trial passes both. (5) pytest tests/test_consistency_graders.py covers all four and passes.

features.description: Operational-validity grader — a rendered command must be accepted by its target in dry-run, not merely parse cleanly
steps: For each command a trial rendered, resolve its target handler and confirm the handler accepts it in a dry-run or preview mode
Report token-shape validity and operational validity as two separate verdicts on the same command, so a divergence between them is visible rather than collapsed
Seed the fixture from the recorded case: a close command rendered against a plan whose status was not active, which passed token validation and would have raised at runtime
A command the grader cannot dry-run safely is reported not-applicable, never assumed valid
No command is ever executed for real by the grader
features.acceptance: (1) The recorded non-active close case is passed by the token check and failed by the operational check, and the report shows both. (2) A close command rendered against an active all-passing plan passes both checks. (3) A command whose handler exposes no safe dry-run is reported not-applicable rather than passing. (4) A monkeypatched execution path proves no command is executed for real during grading. (5) pytest tests/test_operational_validity_grader.py covers all four and passes.

features.description: Judge grader for narrative quality, opt-in and rubric-versioned so a score is reproducible against a known rubric
steps: Store the judge prompt and its rubric as versioned artifacts under the plan's evidence directory, not inline in source
Stamp the rubric version into every judged result so historical scores remain interpretable after a rubric edit
Judge two things only in v0: whether a decision entry's rationale gives a reason rather than restating the decision, and whether an audit summary's prose agrees with its structured verdict
The judge is never invoked unless explicitly enabled; a report produced without it says so rather than omitting the dimension silently
Where a deterministic detector already exists for a dimension, the deterministic result wins and the judge is advisory
features.acceptance: (1) A default run performs no model call, asserted by a monkeypatched executor that raises if invoked. (2) A report produced without the judge names the dimensions it did not evaluate. (3) Every judged result carries the rubric version. (4) On a decision entry whose rationale restates the decision, the judge's verdict and reason are recorded, whatever they are, rather than being discarded. (5) Where the existing verdict-mismatch detector and the judge disagree, the deterministic result is the one reported as authoritative. (6) pytest tests/test_judge_grader.py covers all five and passes.

features.description: Judge calibration against a human-labeled subset, reported as an agreement rate with its sample size
steps: Assemble a labeled subset by hand from existing audit envelopes and decision entries already in the repository
Record each label with who assigned it and when, so the ground truth is attributable rather than anonymous
Run the judge over the subset and report agreement, disagreement, and the cases where they diverge in full
Report the sample size next to the rate everywhere the rate appears
State plainly in the report that an agreement rate over a subset this size is an indication, not a guarantee
features.acceptance: (1) The calibration report states the agreement rate and the labeled-set size adjacent to each other. (2) Every divergent case is listed with both verdicts and both reasons. (3) Every label names its assigner and date. (4) The report contains an explicit statement of what the sample size does and does not support. (5) Re-running the judge over the same subset with the same rubric version reproduces the same agreement rate.

features.description: Seed corpus reconstructed from recorded failures, each scenario citing its source incident and stating intended behavior independently of current behavior
steps: Reconstruct scenarios from the recorded 2026-08-09 cases: a plan whose Target section carried prose instead of the required fenced block; a plan whose acceptance criteria collapsed to a single criterion and tripped the pre-lock size heuristics; an approval that cleared a gate and left the feature unflipped with no signoff; a dispatch blocked by unrelated dirty state
Reconstruct the recorded 2026-07-30 verdict case, where an audit whose subject vocabulary contained a status word was misclassified and contributed to a global breaker trip

Reconstruct the 2026-08-09 signoff-circularity case: a volley writes its own INBOX, audit envelopes, transcript, and git-state evidence, then the patch-completeness check at signoff classifies those same freshly-written artifacts as unrelated dirty state and blocks the signoff — so a run cannot complete without an operator override or a prior commit of files the run itself just created
Each scenario file names the incident it came from and the date, so provenance survives the person who wrote it
Each scenario states the intended behavior in its own words, separately from whatever the system does today, so a scenario may legitimately fail against the current implementation
Report the share of the corpus drawn from any single incident or session, per D006
features.acceptance: (1) Every corpus scenario names a source incident with a date. (2) Every corpus scenario states intended behavior in a field distinct from expected current behavior. (3) At least one scenario fails against the current implementation, is marked as expected-to-fail with a reason, and does not count as a harness error. (4) The corpus report states the share contributed by the largest single source. (5) Running the whole corpus produces a per-scenario result table with no scenario erroring out.

features.description: Documented promotion path from a real failure to a corpus scenario, so the corpus grows from operations rather than invention
steps: Write the loop: an observed failure becomes an incident note, the note becomes a scenario with provenance, the scenario enters the corpus, and the corpus result is reported
Name the artifacts a failure must carry before it is promotable — at minimum a trigger, an observed behavior, and an intended behavior
State the anti-pattern explicitly: writing a scenario and its grader in the same sitting produces a test that asserts the code does what the code does
Reference the guidance from the plan-artifacts skill so it reaches authors at writing time
Record where the corpus lives and how a contributor adds to it without touching harness source
features.acceptance: (1) The guidance exists and names the three artifacts a failure must carry to be promotable. (2) The guidance states the same-sitting anti-pattern explicitly. (3) The plan-artifacts skill references it. (4) A reader following only the guidance can add a scenario without editing any file under the orchestrator package, demonstrated by adding one. (5) The added scenario runs in the corpus.
